_comment: Banner templates matched by appearance, because Windows OCR cannot read
these games' stylised display fonts at all - 'TRIPLE KILL' reads back as
'&fR/PlfWlEo', and 'TEAM KILL!' and 'VICTORY ROYALE' as nothing. Upscaling,
contrast and inversion do not help. Correlating against a reference does:
a matching banner scores ~0.97, a different banner in the same place ~0.50,
'region' is [x, y, width, height] as fractions of the FULL 1920x1080 frame -
the same coordinate system as DetectorRegions - and is converted to a crop
inside its slot at load. 'slot' is which of the three HUD crops it lives in.
The region is a SEARCH BAND, deliberately taller than the banner: Fortnite
stacks these, so 'ELIMINATION!' alone sits ~20px lower than 'DOUBLE ELIM!'
with an 'ENEMY TEAM WIPED!' above it. The matcher slides the template down
the band and takes the best score.
Templates are greyscale so they compare directly against the capture's
luminance plane, and are rescaled at match time, so a 1080p reference still
matches a 1440p capture. Capture them with ffmpeg's -accurate_seek, or fast
seek lands on a neighbouring keyframe and you bank the wrong banner.
Plain HUD text - Overwatch's elimination rows, Fortnite's kill feed - is
still read by OCR. Only the stylised banners are matched this way.
